From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. # Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Before the substance: how the package is framed

The Seller's package tries to narrow our review in three ways. None of them binds us.

- **"[STANDARD]" tags and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note."** The Seller says clauses tagged [STANDARD] were "reviewed and cleared by both sides" and that we should look only at [OPEN] items. Nothing in the package is tagged [OPEN], so on its terms we would review nothing. Almost every [STANDARD] item departs materially from our playbook. These labels are the Seller's own categorisation. I have reviewed every clause on its merits.
- **"Settled at principal level … FINAL."** We have no record of any principal-level agreement. Under the playbook, the 20% cap and the 18-month claims period are fallbacks that need Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying this draft. None has been given. Unless Amelia confirms otherwise in writing, we treat these positions as unagreed.
- **"Market context."** The claims about market-standard caps, baskets and periods are advocacy, not evidence. They do not change our positions.

**Recommendation:** Say in our cover note that we do not accept the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] categorisation or any suggestion that terms are agreed, and that all clauses remain open to mark-up.

---

## Clause-by-clause departures and pushback

### 1. General Warranty cap (cl 12.1)
- **Seller:** 20% / AUD 4.8m.
- **Playbook:** 25% / AUD 6.0m.
- **Issue:** The Seller is offering our conditional fallback as its opening position, presented as already agreed. We have no authority to concede it.
- **Push back:** Reinstate 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not mention the fallback.

### 2. Thresholds (cl 12.2)
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, with only the excess recoverable (a deductible).
- **Playbook:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Basket AUD 50,000, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded (a tipping basket).
- **Issue:** The de minimis is 5× ours and the basket is 5× ours. The deductible also permanently removes the first AUD 250k of losses. Combined with the higher de minimis, a series of mid-sized claims could become unrecoverable.
- **Push back:** AUD 5k / AUD 50k, tipping basket.

### 3. Time limits (cl 12.3 / 13)
- **Seller:** 18 months. Any limitation also applies to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise."
- **Playbook:** 24 months for general claims. 18 months is an unauthorised fallback.
- **Issue:** The "all Claims" wording is a hidden override of the general regime. It would pull Title, Tax, IP, indemnity, payment and covenant claims under the 18-month bar by default.
- **Push back:** 24 months for general Warranty Claims only. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default. Each category gets its own express regime.

### 4. Fundamental / Title
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties fall under the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity."
- **Playbook:** A separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
- **Issue:** This is a fundamental departure. Title to 100% of the shares is the core of the deal. Capping it at AUD 4.8m on an AUD 24m price is unacceptable.
- **Push back:** Reject. Reinstate the separate Fundamental regime.

### 5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5)
- **Seller:** These apply to "all Claims of any nature."
- **Playbook:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This is non-waivable.
- **Issue:** As drafted, this could be argued to shield Seller fraud. That is our most important non-negotiable.
- **Push back:** Add an express overriding carve-out, plus a carve-out for the Fundamental, Tax, IP and specific indemnity regimes.

### 6. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records."
- **Playbook:** Specific fair disclosure only. Reject data-room, public-register or deemed-search disclosure.
- **Issues:**
  - The general disclosure would cut back every warranty.
  - The data room cut-off is 22 September 2026, more than six weeks ago. A current bring-down is needed.
  - Letter 1.4 ("nothing admits … that any consent … is legally required") is acceptable as a non-admission. However, it must not be read as qualifying the warranties themselves.
- **Push back:** Delete 1.1 and 1.2. Only matters "fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to enable the Buyer to identify the nature and scope" in the specific paragraphs qualify the warranties. No disclosure against Title or Capacity warranties. Require an updated letter at Completion, with no new disclosure against warranties repeated at Completion without our consent.

### 7. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was discoverable from the data room or public records.
- **Playbook:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must be limited to named persons with reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Issue:** The "discoverable" wording is constructive knowledge. It is broader even than the general disclosure, and it would undermine the specific indemnities we are taking for known issues (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses).
- **Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a Seller-knowledge qualifier: named Seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry.

### 8. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours, with the condition satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered.
- **Playbook:** Require an effective consent and evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery and reasonable endeavours alone are not enough.
- **Why it matters:** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue. Its consent is subject to conditions in DD-002 cl 11.3, and the Seller confirms it has neither a final consent nor evidence that the conditions are met (Letter para 2).
- **Push back:**
  - A condition precedent to Completion: an unconditional (or conditions-satisfied), effective written consent under cl 11.2, with documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - A best/all-reasonable-endeavours obligation on the Seller to procure it.
  - The CP waivable by the Buyer only.

### 9. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)
- **Seller:** A release "to be provided following Completion."
- **Playbook:** A current payout figure, repayment directly from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Why it matters:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the facility has change-of-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions. It has not been repaid and no discharge exists (Letter para 3). On a debt-free basis this must come out of the price. Without a release we could acquire an encumbered company in default.
- **Push back:**
  - A payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Direct payment to Riverlark in the funds flow, deducted as Debt.
  - Executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion.
- **Fallback:** Do not offer the post-completion fallback without Amelia's approval.

### 10. Funds flow: DD-005 bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Playbook:** The AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Issue:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion. If not provided for, the Company (and so we) pays them after Completion. The Seller also does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply (Letter para 5).
- **Push back:** Treat the AUD 420k plus all associated on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding mechanics) as Debt or Transaction Costs, deducted in the funds flow. Alternatively, have them paid from Seller proceeds. Back this with a specific indemnity outside the general regime.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."
- **Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
- **Issue:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment (Letter para 4). The exposure is the IP itself, not just the fee: ownership, third-party claims, and the cost of re-development or a licence.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the Ironquay deliverables, including SOW3 materials.
  - Keep a CP or pre-Completion cure: verified settlement of the SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Do not adopt AUD 180k as an agreed figure in either direction. It comes from DD-010 and is not bank-verified. Require independent verification.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sched 6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Issue:** The "not expected to be material" statement is an unsupported characterisation. Our position is equally neutral: the facts are unknown.
- **Push back:** Delete the materiality statement. Add:
  - pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation, and give the Buyer regular written updates and access;
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision under the Privacy Act / NDB scheme;
  - a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, outside the general basket and cap, without assuming any breach or quantum.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** Assess them. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Issue:** The disclosure itself says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course (Letter para 8). It also says DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together, which suggests a possibly related or split arrangement.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the Seller's label. Raise due diligence requests on terms, approvals, termination rights, timing and accrual. Decide on treatment (ordinary-course carve-out, Debt, conduct-of-business restriction, or none) once the facts are known. Do not pre-empt this with a deduction demand.

### 14. Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** These remain open. Assume no resolution and no unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** Record them as open. Keep separate Tax and IP regimes, with their own caps, periods and indemnity mechanics, to be negotiated. Do not let them fall into the general regime through the cl 12.3 "all Claims" default.

### 15. Title evidence
- **Seller:** Title "is evidenced by" the DD-012 share register.
- **Playbook:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source.
- **Issue:** The Seller concedes in Letter para 10 that DD-012 only identifies its source and does not mean we have verified title.
- **Push back:** Require the following, plus an unqualified Title warranty under the Fundamental regime:
  - a current ASIC company extract reconciled to the register;
  - share certificates;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or rights exist over the shares;
  - Seller board resolutions and authority evidence;
  - a security release over the shares (linked to Riverlark).

### 16. Other items to close out (not in the playbook, but worth noting)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** A notification obligation only. Make sure notice is given on time and add a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** An assignment restriction that does not on its face catch a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording elsewhere in the contract.
- **Stale disclosure date:** The cut-off of 22 September 2026 needs a current bring-down.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller | Our position |
|---|---|---|---|
| – | Framing | [STANDARD] means cleared; "FINAL" | Reject. All clauses open; no principal agreement on record |
| 1 | Cap | 20% / 4.8m | **25% / AUD 6.0m** (no fallback authority) |
| 2 | Thresholds | 25k / 250k deductible | **5k / 50k tipping** |
| 3 | Claims period | 18m; applies to all Claims | **24m, general warranties only**; delete override |
| 4 | Title/Capacity | General regime | **100% cap, ≥6 yrs, outside basket/knowledge** |
| 5 | Fraud | Limits apply to all | **Full fraud/wilful concealment/misconduct carve-out** (non-negotiable) |
| 6 | Disclosure | Data room + public records | **Specific fair disclosure only**; updated letter |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Blanket + "discoverable" | **Delete** |
| 8 | Bluefen | Reasonable endeavours, consent on delivery | **CP: effective consent + evidence that cl 11.3 conditions are met** |
| 9 | Riverlark | Post-Completion release | **Payout letter, direct repayment, releases at Completion** |
| 10 | Bonuses | Not itemised | **AUD 420k + on-costs as a line item / Seller-funded + indemnity** |
| 11 | Ironquay | SOW3 payment only | **Broadened IP indemnity + SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified** |
| 12 | DD-006 | "Not material" | **Delete characterisation; preservation, investigation and update covenants; neutral indemnity** |
| 13 | Sandbar | Ordinary course | **Diligence first; no automatic Debt/deduction** |
| 14 | Tax/IP | Settled under general regime | **Open; separate regimes** |
| 15 | Title | DD-012 register | **Independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, authority)** |

**Escalation:** Two of the Seller's positions match our unauthorised fallbacks: the 20% cap and the 18-month period. The Seller also says these were settled at principal level. I recommend confirming directly with Amelia Frost that she has given no such agreement or authority before we send the mark-up. If she wants to authorise either fallback, she must do so in writing, identifying this draft.

- **Why it matters:** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding, and the facility has change-of-control (cl 8.1) and discharge (cl 9.2) provisions. It has not been repaid and no discharge exists (Letter para 3). On a debt-free basis this must come out of the price. Without a release we could acquire an encumbered company in default.
- **Push back:**
  - A payout letter dated close to Completion.
  - Direct payment to Riverlark in the funds flow, deducted as Debt.
  - Executed deeds of release and PPSR discharges delivered at Completion.
- **Fallback:** Do not offer the post-completion fallback without Amelia's approval.

### 10. Funds flow: DD-005 bonuses
- **Seller:** AUD 420,000 in bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised.
- **Playbook:** The AUD 420k plus any triggered on-costs must be a specific line item or Seller-funded. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Issue:** The bonuses are triggered by Completion. If not provided for, the Company (and so we) pays them after Completion. The Seller also does not say whether payroll tax, superannuation or other on-costs apply (Letter para 5).
- **Push back:** Treat the AUD 420k plus all associated on-costs (payroll tax, super, PAYG withholding mechanics) as Debt or Transaction Costs, deducted in the funds flow. Alternatively, have them paid from Seller proceeds. Back this with a specific indemnity outside the general regime.

### 11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment and is "considered adequate."
- **Playbook:** Broaden the indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
- **Issue:** Under DD-004 cl 7.3, transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials depends on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. There is no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment (Letter para 4). The exposure is the IP itself, not just the fee: ownership, third-party claims, and the cost of re-development or a licence.
- **Push back:**
  - Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own or have the right to use the Ironquay deliverables, including SOW3 materials.
  - Keep a CP or pre-Completion cure: verified settlement of the SOW3 fees and an executed confirmatory assignment from Ironquay.
  - Do not adopt AUD 180k as an agreed figure in either direction. It comes from DD-010 and is not bank-verified. Require independent verification.

### 12. DD-006 export/privacy incident (cl 4.6 / Sched 6)
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter … not expected to be material."
- **Playbook:** Preserve logs, investigate and require updates. Assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- **Issue:** The "not expected to be material" statement is an unsupported characterisation. Our position is equally neutral: the facts are unknown.
- **Push back:** Delete the materiality statement. Add:
  - pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs and evidence, continue a proper investigation, and give the Buyer regular written updates and access;
  - Buyer consultation on any notification decision under the Privacy Act / NDB scheme;
  - a specific indemnity for losses arising from the incident, outside the general basket and cap, without assuming any breach or quantum.

### 13. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)
- **Seller:** "Ordinary-course operating costs."
- **Playbook:** Assess them. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Issue:** The disclosure itself says it does not state whether the renewals are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course (Letter para 8). It also says DD-008 and DD-011 must be read together, which suggests a possibly related or split arrangement.
- **Push back:** Do not accept the Seller's label. Raise due diligence requests on terms, approvals, termination rights, timing and accrual. Decide on treatment (ordinary-course carve-out, Debt, conduct-of-business restriction, or none) once the facts are known. Do not pre-empt this with a deduction demand.

### 14. Tax and IP warranties
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime."
- **Playbook:** These remain open. Assume no resolution and no unlimited liability.
- **Push back:** Record them as open. Keep separate Tax and IP regimes, with their own caps, periods and indemnity mechanics, to be negotiated. Do not let them fall into the general regime through the cl 12.3 "all Claims" default.

### 15. Title evidence
- **Seller:** Title "is evidenced by" the DD-012 share register.
- **Playbook:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. DD-012 is an internal source.
- **Issue:** The Seller concedes in Letter para 10 that DD-012 only identifies its source and does not mean we have verified title.
- **Push back:** Require the following, plus an unqualified Title warranty under the Fundamental regime:
  - a current ASIC company extract reconciled to the register;
  - share certificates;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
  - confirmation that no options, convertibles or rights exist over the shares;
  - Seller board resolutions and authority evidence;
  - a security release over the shares (linked to Riverlark).

### 16. Other items to close out (not in the playbook, but worth noting)
- **Office lease (DD-007):** A notification obligation only. Make sure notice is given on time and add a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** An assignment restriction that does not on its face catch a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment wording elsewhere in the contract.
- **Stale disclosure date:** The cut-off of 22 September 2026 needs a current bring-down.
